sentences.zh: 南齊書卷三十二‧列傳第十三

translations.literal: Book of the Southern Qi, Volume 32 — Biography 13
translations.idiomatic: Book of the Southern Qi, Volume 32 — Biography 13

sentences.zh: 王琨 張岱 褚炫 何戢 王延之 阮韜

translations.literal: Wang Kun; Zhang Dai; Chu Xuan; He Ji; Wang Yanzhi; Ruan Tao
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kun; Zhang Dai; Chu Xuan; He Ji; Wang Yanzhi; Ruan Tao

sentences.zh: 王琨，琅邪臨沂人也。

translations.literal: Wang Kun was a native of Linyi in Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kun was a man of Linyi in Langye.

sentences.zh: 祖薈，晉衞將軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hui was a Jin guard general.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hui had been a guard general under the Jin.

sentences.zh: 父懌，不慧，侍婢生琨，名爲崑崙。

translations.literal: His father Yi was dull-witted; a serving maid bore Kun, and he was named Kunlun.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yi was dull of wit; a serving maid bore Kun, and the boy was named Kunlun.

sentences.zh: 懌後娶南陽樂玄女，無子，改琨名，立以爲嗣。

translations.literal: Later Yi married a daughter of Yue Xuan of Nanyang; having no son, he changed Kun's name and established him as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yi married a daughter of Yue Xuan of Nanyang; when she bore no son, he changed Kun's name and set him up as heir.

sentences.zh: 琨少謹篤，爲從伯司徒謐所愛。

translations.literal: Kun from youth was careful and steadfast, and was beloved by his father's cousin, Grand Steward Mi.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Kun was careful and steadfast, and his father's cousin Grand Steward Mi doted on him.

sentences.zh: 宋永初中，武帝以其娶桓脩女，除郎中，駙馬都尉，奉朝請。

translations.literal: In the beginning of the Yongchu era under Song, Emperor Wu, because Kun had married the daughter of Huan Xiu, appointed him gentleman of the palace, commandant-escort for the imperial son-in-law, and attendant at court.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Song Yongchu era, Emperor Wu, because Kun had married Huan Xiu's daughter, named him gentleman of the palace, commandant-escort for the imperial son-in-law, and attendant at court.

sentences.zh: 元嘉初，從兄侍中華有權寵，以門戶衰弱，待琨如親，數相稱薦。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanjia his cousin Hua, attendant-in-chief, held power and favor; because the family standing was weak, he treated Kun as kin and often spoke him up for recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanjia his cousin Hua, attendant-in-chief, held power and favor; with the clan's standing enfeebled, he treated Kun as close kin and often praised him for office.

sentences.zh: 爲尚書儀曹郎，州治中。

translations.literal: He became a gentleman in the ministry of rites' ceremony bureau and provincial aide.
translations.idiomatic: He became a gentleman in the ministry of rites' ceremony bureau and a provincial aide.

sentences.zh: 累至左軍諮議，領錄事，出爲宣城太守，司徒從事中郎，義興太守。

translations.literal: He rose in stages to left-army adviser, with charge as recording aide, then went out as administrator of Xuancheng, gentleman-attendant of the grand steward, and administrator of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose by stages to left-army adviser, leading the recording aide, then went out as administrator of Xuancheng, gentleman-attendant of the grand steward, and administrator of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 歷任皆廉約。

translations.literal: In every post he was frugal and sparing.
translations.idiomatic: In every post he was frugal and sparing.

sentences.zh: 還爲北中郎長史，黃門郎，寧朔將軍，東陽太守。

translations.literal: He returned to serve as chief clerk of the northern central commandant, gentleman of the yellow gate, general who stills the north, and administrator of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as chief clerk of the northern central commandant, gentleman of the yellow gate, general who stills the north, and administrator of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 孝建初，遷廷尉卿，竟陵王驃騎長史，加臨淮太守，轉吏部郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaojian he was moved to director of the court of justice, chief clerk to Prince of Jingling's grand marshal, with added duty as administrator of Linhuai, then transferred to director of the ministry of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Xiaojian he was moved to director of the court of justice, chief clerk to Prince of Jingling's grand marshal, with added duty as administrator of Linhuai, then transferred to director of the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 吏曹選局，貴要多所屬請，琨自公卿下至士大夫，例爲用兩門生。

translations.literal: In the personnel bureau's selection office the powerful often submitted requests on behalf of others; Kun, from grand ministers down to gentlemen-scholars, as a rule employed only two local recruits.
translations.idiomatic: In the personnel bureau's selection office the great often pressed requests for their clients; Kun, from grand ministers down to gentlemen-scholars, as a rule took on only two local recruits.

sentences.zh: 江夏王義恭嘗屬琨用二人，後復遣屬琨，答不許。

translations.literal: Prince of Jiangxia Yigong once asked Kun to employ two men; later he sent another request, and Kun answered that he would not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jiangxia Yigong once asked Kun to place two men; when he sent the request again, Kun refused.

sentences.zh: 出爲持節、都督廣交二州軍事、建威將軍、平越將軍、平越中郎將、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out bearing the staff, as supervisor of military affairs for the two provinces of Guang and Jiao, general who establishes might, general who pacifies Yue, middle-rank commandant who pacifies Yue, and inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He went out bearing the staff, as supervisor of military affairs for Guang and Jiao, general who establishes might, general who pacifies Yue, middle-rank commandant who pacifies Yue, and inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 南土沃實，在任者常致巨富，世云「廣州刺史但經城門一過，便得三千万」也。

translations.literal: The south was rich land; those who held office there commonly amassed great wealth. A saying ran, 「Every inspector of Guangzhou need only pass once through the city gate to gain thirty million.」
translations.idiomatic: The south was rich country; those who held office there commonly grew fabulously wealthy. People said, 「An inspector of Guangzhou need only pass once through the city gate to gain thirty million.」

sentences.zh: 琨無所取納，表獻祿俸之半。

translations.literal: Kun took nothing for himself and memorialized that he offered half his salary stipend.
translations.idiomatic: Kun took nothing for himself and memorialized that he turned over half his salary.

sentences.zh: 州鎮舊有鼓吹，又啓輸還。

translations.literal: The provincial garrison had long had military music; he also memorialized to return it.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial garrison had long kept a military band; he memorialized to send that back as well.

sentences.zh: 及罷任，孝武知其清，問還資多少？

translations.literal: When his term ended, Emperor Xiaowu, knowing his integrity, asked how much wealth he was bringing back.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended, Emperor Xiaowu, knowing how clean he was, asked how much he was bringing home.

sentences.zh: 琨曰：「臣買宅百三十萬，餘物稱之。

translations.literal: Kun said: 「Your servant bought a house for 1.3 million; the rest matches that.
translations.idiomatic: Kun said: 「Your servant bought a house for 1.3 million; the rest matches that.

sentences.zh: 」帝悅其對。

translations.literal: 」The emperor was pleased with his reply.
translations.idiomatic: 」The emperor was pleased with his reply.

sentences.zh: 爲廷尉，加給事中，轉寧朔將軍長史、歷陽內史。

translations.literal: He was made director of the court of justice, with added duty as cadet within the establishment, then transferred to chief clerk to the general who stills the north and interior administrator of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made director of the court of justice, with added duty as cadet within the establishment, then transferred to chief clerk to the general who stills the north and interior administrator of Liyang.

sentences.zh: 上以琨忠實，徙爲寵子新安王東中郎長史，加輔國將軍，遷右衞將軍，度支尚書。

translations.literal: The emperor, knowing Kun was loyal and true, moved him to chief clerk on the eastern-rank staff of the favored prince, Prince of Xin'an, with added duty as general who assists the state, then moved him to general of the right guard and director of the revenue bureau.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, finding Kun loyal and true, moved him to chief clerk on the eastern-rank staff of the favored Prince of Xin'an, with added duty as general who assists the state, then to general of the right guard and director of the revenue bureau.

sentences.zh: 出爲永嘉王左軍、始安王征虜二府長史，加輔國將軍、廣陵太守，皆孝武諸子。

translations.literal: He went out as chief clerk on the left-army staff of Prince of Yongjia and the campaigning staff of Prince of Shi'an, with added duty as general who assists the state and administrator of Guangling—both were sons of Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as chief clerk on Prince of Yongjia's left-army staff and Prince of Shi'an's campaigning staff, with added duty as general who assists the state and administrator of Guangling—both were sons of Emperor Xiaowu.

sentences.zh: 泰始元年，遷度支尚書，尋加光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taishi he was moved to director of the revenue bureau, and soon after was given the added title grand master for splendid virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taishi he was moved to director of the revenue bureau, and soon after was given the added title grand master for splendid virtue.

sentences.zh: 初，從兄華孫長襲華爵爲新建侯，嗜酒多諐失。

translations.literal: Earlier, his cousin's grandson Chang had inherited Hua's title as Marquis of Xinjian; he was addicted to wine and guilty of many faults.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier his cousin's grandson Chang had inherited Hua's marquisate of Xinjian; he was a drunkard and piled up fault upon fault.

sentences.zh: 琨上表曰：「臣門姪不休，從孫長是故左衞將軍嗣息，少資常猥，猶冀晚進。

translations.literal: Kun memorialized: 「Your servant's clansman's son will not reform; your servant's collateral grandson Chang is the surviving heir of the former left guard general—from youth his means were scant and his conduct coarse, yet one still hoped he might improve in time.
translations.idiomatic: Kun memorialized: 「Your servant's clansman's son will not reform; your servant's collateral grandson Chang is the surviving heir of the former left guard general—from youth his means were scant and his conduct coarse, yet one still hoped he might improve in time.

sentences.zh: 頃更昏酣，業身無檢。

translations.literal: In recent times he has sunk deeper into drunken stupor, and in his person he observes no discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Of late he has sunk deeper into drunken stupor, and his person knows no restraint.

sentences.zh: 故衞將軍華忠肅奉國，善及世祀；

translations.literal: The late guard general Hua was loyal and solemn in serving the state, and his good name reached the sacrifices of generations;
translations.idiomatic: The late guard general Hua was loyal and solemn in serving the state, and his good name reached the sacrifices of generations;

sentences.zh: 而長負釁承封，將傾基緒。

translations.literal: yet Chang bears guilt and inherits the fief; he is about to overturn the foundation and succession.
translations.idiomatic: yet Chang bears guilt and inherits the fief; he is about to overturn the foundation and succession.

sentences.zh: 嗣小息佟閑立保退，不乖素風，如蒙拯立，則存亡荷榮，私祿更搆。」

translations.literal: The heir's young son Tong, nurtured in quiet retirement, does not stray from the family's wont; if he might be rescued and established, then survival and extinction would owe their glory to grace, and private stipend would take a new form.」
translations.idiomatic: The heir's young son Tong, raised in unhurried withdrawal, does not stray from the family's wont; if he might be rescued and established, then survival and extinction would owe their glory to grace, and private stipend would take a new form.」

sentences.zh: 出爲冠軍將軍、吳郡太守，遷中領軍。

translations.literal: He went out as general who commands champions and administrator of Wu commandery, then was moved to general of the central guard.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as general who commands champions and administrator of Wu, then was moved to general of the central guard.

sentences.zh: 坐在郡用朝舍錢三十六萬營餉二宮諸王及作絳襖奉獻軍用，左遷光祿大夫，尋加太常及金紫，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Because while in the commandery he had used 360,000 of the court lodging funds to provision the two palaces' princes and to make crimson jackets as a military offering, he was demoted to grand master for splendid virtue; soon after he was given the added titles grand minister of ceremonies and golden battle-axe with purple trim, and additional gentleman attendant-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Because in the commandery he had spent 360,000 in court lodging funds to provision the two palaces' princes and to make crimson jackets as a military offering, he was demoted to grand master for splendid virtue; soon after he was given the added titles grand minister of ceremonies and golden battle-axe with purple trim, and additional gentleman attendant-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 廷尉虞龢議社稷合爲一神，琨案舊糾駮。

translations.literal: Court of justice director Yu He argued that the altars of soil and grain should be combined into one deity; Kun investigated precedent and impeached the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Court of justice director Yu He argued that the altars of soil and grain should be merged into one god; Kun searched the precedents and impeached him.

sentences.zh: 時龢深被親寵，朝廷多琨強正。

translations.literal: At the time He was deeply favored; the court often found Kun forceful and upright.
translations.idiomatic: At the time He was deeply favored; the court often found Kun forceful and upright.

sentences.zh: 明帝臨崩，出爲督會稽東陽新安臨海永嘉五郡軍事、左軍將軍、會稽太守，常侍如故。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming lay dying, Kun was sent out as supervisor of military affairs for the five commanderies of Kuaiji, Dongyang, Xin'an, Linhai, and Yongjia, general of the left army, and administrator of Kuaiji, attendant-in-chief unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming lay dying, Kun was sent out as supervisor of military affairs for Kuaiji, Dongyang, Xin'an, Linhai, and Yongjia, general of the left army, and administrator of Kuaiji, attendant unchanged.

sentences.zh: 坐誤竟囚，降號冠軍。

translations.literal: Because of an error involving a prisoner who had completed his sentence, he was reduced in rank to general who commands champions.
translations.idiomatic: For an error involving a prisoner whose term had run out, he was reduced in rank to general who commands champions.

sentences.zh: 元徽中，遷金紫光祿，弘訓太僕，常侍如故。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhui era he was moved to golden battle-axe with splendid-virtue grand master, grand coachman of glorious instruction, attendant unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhui era he was moved to golden battle-axe with splendid-virtue grand master, grand coachman of glorious instruction, attendant unchanged.

sentences.zh: 本州中正，加特進。

translations.literal: He was comparison bureau chief for his home province, with added extraordinary promotion.
translations.idiomatic: He was comparison bureau chief for his home province, with added extraordinary promotion.

sentences.zh: 從帝卽位，進右光祿大夫，常侍餘如故。

translations.literal: When the deposed emperor took the throne, Kun was advanced to grand master for splendid virtue of the right, attendancies otherwise unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: When the deposed emperor took the throne, Kun was advanced to right splendid-virtue grand master, his attendancies otherwise unchanged.

sentences.zh: 從帝遜位，琨陪位及辭廟，皆流涕。

translations.literal: When the deposed emperor yielded the throne, Kun was present at the investiture and at the farewell at the ancestral temple, and wept both times.
translations.idiomatic: When the deposed emperor yielded the throne, Kun was present at the investiture and at the farewell at the ancestral temple, and wept both times.

sentences.zh: 太祖卽位，領武陵王師，加侍中，給親信二十人。

translations.literal: When the Founder took the throne, Kun led Prince of Wuling's tutoring staff, with added attendant-in-chief, and was given twenty intimate guardsmen.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder took the throne, Kun led Prince of Wuling's tutoring staff, with added attendant-in-chief, and was given twenty intimate guardsmen.

sentences.zh: 時王儉爲宰相，屬琨用東海郡迎吏。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Jian was prime minister and asked Kun to employ the welcome officer of Donghai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wang Jian was prime minister and asked Kun to place the welcome officer of Donghai commandery.

sentences.zh: 琨謂信人曰：「語郎，三臺五省，皆是郎用人；

translations.literal: Kun told a trusted man: 「Tell the gentleman: the Three Platforms and Five Bureaus are all places where the gentleman places his men;
translations.idiomatic: Kun told a trusted man: 「Tell the gentleman: the Three Platforms and Five Bureaus are all places where the gentleman places his men;

sentences.zh: 外方小郡，當乞寒賤，省官何容復奪之。

translations.literal: a petty outer commandery ought to beg for someone humble and poor—how can a court officer be allowed to seize him again?
translations.idiomatic: a petty outer commandery ought to beg for someone humble and poor—how can a court officer be allowed to seize him again?

sentences.zh: 」遂不過其事。

translations.literal: 」And so he did not forward the matter.
translations.idiomatic: 」And so he did not forward the matter.

sentences.zh: 琨性旣古慎，而儉嗇過甚，家人雜事，皆手自操執。

translations.literal: By nature Kun was old-fashioned and cautious, yet his thrift went too far; household chores great and small, he handled himself.
translations.idiomatic: By nature Kun was old-fashioned and cautious, yet his thrift went too far; great and small household chores he did with his own hands.

sentences.zh: 公事朝會，必夙夜早起，簡閱衣裳，料數冠幘，如此數四，世以此笑之。

translations.literal: For public business and court assemblies he always rose early at night, checked his garments, reckoned caps and kerchiefs—thus several times over; the age laughed at him for it.
translations.idiomatic: For public business and court assemblies he always rose in the deep of night, inspected his garments, counted caps and kerchiefs—thus several times over—and the age laughed at him for it.

sentences.zh: 尋解王師。

translations.literal: Soon he was released from duties as preceptor to the prince.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was relieved of his post as tutor to the prince.

sentences.zh: 建元四年，太祖崩，琨聞國諱，牛不在宅，去臺數里，遂步行入宮。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianyuan the founding emperor died; Kun heard the national mourning, his ox was not at the house, and though the court lay several li away he walked into the palace on foot.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyuan year four the founding emperor died. When Kun heard the mourning edict, his cart ox was away from home; the court stood several li off, yet he walked in on foot.

sentences.zh: 朝士皆謂琨曰：「故宜待車，有損國望。

translations.literal: Court gentlemen all told Kun, 「You should have waited for a carriage after all; it damages the state's dignity.
translations.idiomatic: Men at court all told Kun, 「You ought to have waited for your carriage; it hurts the dignity of the realm.

sentences.zh: 」琨曰：「今日奔赴，皆應爾。

translations.literal: 」Kun said, 「Today's rush to attend—everyone should act thus.
translations.idiomatic: 」Kun said, 「On a day like this, every man should do the same.

sentences.zh: 」遂得病，卒。

translations.literal: 」Thereupon he fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: 」He fell ill on the spot and died.

sentences.zh: 贈左光祿大夫，餘如故。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Left Household Minister with the Golden Seal; the rest of his honors stood as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made left household minister with the golden seal; his other honors were left unchanged.

sentences.zh: 年八十四。

translations.literal: He was eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He was eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 張岱字景山，吳郡吳人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Dai, styled Jingshan, was a native of Wu in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dai, styled Jingshan, came from Wu in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖敞，晉度支尚書，父茂度，宋金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chang was revenue superintendent of Jin; his father Maodu was household minister with the purple-gold seal under the Song.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chang had been Jin revenue superintendent; his father Maodu, a Song household minister with the purple-gold seal.

sentences.zh: 岱少與兄太子中舍人寅、新安太守鏡、征北將軍永、弟廣州刺史辨俱知名，謂之張氏五龍。

translations.literal: In youth Dai, with his elder brother Yin, crown prince household court gentleman, Jing, administrator of Xin'an, Yong, general who pacifies the north, and his younger brother Bian, administrator of Guangzhou, were all famed; men called them the Five Dragons of the Zhang clan.
translations.idiomatic: Young, Dai and his brothers—Yin, a crown-prince household court gentleman; Jing, administrator of Xin'an; Yong, general who pacifies the north; and the younger Bian, administrator of Guangzhou—were all celebrated; people spoke of the Zhang clan's Five Dragons.

sentences.zh: 鏡少與光祿大夫顏延之隣居，顏談議飲酒，喧呼不絕；

translations.literal: Jing in youth lived next to household minister Yan Yanzhi; Yan would hold drinking debates, clamor and shouting without cease;
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Jing lived beside household minister Yan Yanzhi; Yan held drinking debates that roared on without pause;

sentences.zh: 而鏡靜翳無言聲。

translations.literal: while Jing stayed quiet and gave no sound.
translations.idiomatic: while Jing kept still and never raised his voice.

sentences.zh: 後延之於籬邊聞其與客語，取胡牀坐聽，辭義清玄，延之心服，謂賔客曰：「彼有人焉。

translations.literal: Later Yanzhi heard him talking with guests beyond the fence, took a folding stool and sat to listen; his words were clear and profound, and Yanzhi was won over and said to his guests, 「There is a man there.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yanzhi overheard him speaking with guests beyond the fence, brought a folding stool to sit and listen, and found his words lucid and deep. Yanzhi was convinced and told his guests, 「There is a man over there.

sentences.zh: 」由此不復酣呌。

translations.literal: 」From this he no longer got rowdy drunk.
translations.idiomatic: 」After that he never again drank himself into a racket.

sentences.zh: 寅、鏡名最高，永、辨、岱不及也。

translations.literal: Yin and Jing had the highest fame; Yong, Bian, and Dai did not match them.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and Jing stood highest in renown; Yong, Bian, and Dai could not equal them.

sentences.zh: 郡舉岱上計掾，不行，州辟從事。

translations.literal: The commandery nominated Dai as tribute-accounting clerk; he did not go. The prefecture summoned him as staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery nominated him as tribute-accounting clerk, but he would not go; the prefecture then called him in as a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 累遷南平王右軍主簿，尚書水部郎。

translations.literal: He rose in stages to secretariat clerk of the South Ping prince's right army and gentleman of the ministry's water bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced step by step to secretariat clerk on the South Ping prince's right-army staff and gentleman in the ministry's water bureau.

sentences.zh: 出補東遷令。

translations.literal: He was posted out to serve as magistrate of Dongqian.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to fill the post of magistrate of Dongqian.

sentences.zh: 時殷沖爲吳興，謂人曰：「張東遷親貧須養，所以栖遲下邑。

translations.literal: At the time Yin Chong held Wuxing and said to others, 「Zhang of Dongqian is close to his kin and poor and must support them, hence his delay in a small county.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Chong was then in Wuxing and told others, 「Zhang of Dongqian stays close to kin who are poor and must be fed—that is why he lingers in a small county.

sentences.zh: 然名器方顯，終當大至。」

translations.literal: Yet his name and vessel are just showing; in the end he will reach high office.」
translations.idiomatic: Yet his name and standing are only beginning to show; in the end he will rise very high.」

sentences.zh: 隨王誕於會稽起義，以岱爲建威將軍，輔國長史，行縣事。

translations.literal: When Prince Sui Dan raised arms at Kuaiji, Dai was made general who establishes might, chief of staff who supports the state, and acted in county affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Sui Dan rose in arms at Kuaiji, Dai was named general who establishes might and chief of staff who supports the state, and handled the county's business in his stead.

sentences.zh: 事平，爲司徒左西曹。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he became an officer of the minister of state's left western bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Once the rising was put down he entered the minister of state's left western bureau.

sentences.zh: 母年八十，籍注未滿，岱便去官從實還養，有司以岱違制，將欲糾舉。

translations.literal: His mother was eighty; the household register had not yet been brought up to date, and Dai at once left office and went home in truth to support her. The authorities held that Dai had violated regulations and were about to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was eighty, but the household register had not yet caught up; Dai resigned at once and went home in earnest to care for her. The authorities judged that he had broken the rules and were ready to prosecute.

sentences.zh: 宋孝武曰：「觀過可以知仁，不須案也。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of Song said, 「By watching faults one can know benevolence; there is no need for a case.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu of Song said, 「From a man's lapses you may read his heart; let there be no inquiry.

sentences.zh: 」累遷撫軍諮議參軍，領山陰令，職事閑理。

translations.literal: 」He rose in stages to military advisor on the pacification army staff, concurrently magistrate of Shanyin; his duties were leisurely and well ordered.
translations.idiomatic: 」He advanced to military advisor on the pacification army staff and served concurrently as magistrate of Shanyin, where the work ran calm and clear.

sentences.zh: 巴陵王休若爲北徐州，未親政事，以岱爲冠軍諮議參軍，領彭城太守，行府、州、國事。

translations.literal: Prince Baling Xiuruo held northern Xuzhou but did not personally handle government; Dai was made military advisor of the champion, concurrently administrator of Pengcheng, and acted in the mansion, prefecture, and princedom affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Baling Xiuruo was posted to northern Xuzhou yet did not govern in person; Dai became military advisor of the champion, concurrently administrator of Pengcheng, and ran the mansion, prefecture, and princedom in his stead.

sentences.zh: 後臨海王爲征虜廣州，豫章王爲車騎揚州，晉安王爲征虜南兖州，岱歷爲三府諮議、三王行事，與典籤主帥共事，事舉而情得。

translations.literal: Later the prince of Linhai was pacify-the-far-reaches at Guangzhou, the prince of Yuzhang chariots-and-horses at Yangzhou, and the prince of Jin'an pacify-the-far-reaches at southern Yanzhou; Dai in turn served as advisor to three mansions and chief administrator for three princes, working with registry clerks and chief stewards; affairs were concluded and feelings were accommodated.
translations.idiomatic: Later the prince of Linhai held Guangzhou as pacify-the-far-reaches, the prince of Yuzhang Yangzhou as chariots-and-horses, and the prince of Jin'an southern Yanzhou in the same role; Dai served in turn as advisor to three households and chief administrator for three princes, sharing work with registry clerks and chief stewards until business was finished and tempers stayed smooth.

sentences.zh: 或謂岱曰：「主王旣幼，執事多門，而每能緝和公私，云何致此？

translations.literal: Someone said to Dai, 「The young lords are still young and many hands hold power, yet you each time can harmonize public and private—how do you achieve this?
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked Dai, 「Your lords are still young, and power is split among many officers—yet you always reconcile public duty and private feeling. How do you manage it?

sentences.zh: 」岱曰：「古人言一心可以事百君。

translations.literal: 」Dai said, 「The ancients said one heart can serve a hundred lords.
translations.idiomatic: 」Dai said, 「The ancients said that with one loyal heart a man may serve a hundred masters.

sentences.zh: 我爲政端平，待物以禮，悔吝之事，無由而及。

translations.literal: I govern uprightly and evenly and treat things with ritual; matters of regret have no way to reach me.
translations.idiomatic: I govern straight and even, and meet men with ritual; regret has no door to reach me.

sentences.zh: 明闇短長，更是才用之多少耳。」

translations.literal: Bright and dark, short and long—that is more a matter of how much talent is employed.」
translations.idiomatic: What looks bright or dim, skilled or wanting, is only how much talent the post allows.」

sentences.zh: 入爲黃門郎，遷驃騎長史，領廣陵太守。

translations.literal: He entered court as yellow gate gentleman, moved to chief of staff of the swift cavalry, and concurrently held Guangling as administrator.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as a yellow gate gentleman, then became chief of staff to the swift cavalry and concurrently administrator of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 新安王子鸞以盛寵爲南徐州，割吳郡屬焉。

translations.literal: Prince Xin'an Ziluan, in the height of favor, held southern Xuzhou, and Wu commandery was carved out to belong to it.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xin'an Ziluan, deep in imperial favor, took southern Xuzhou, and Wu commandery was cut away to fall under him.

sentences.zh: 高選佐史，孝武帝召岱謂之曰：「卿美效夙著，兼資宦已多。

translations.literal: High-ranking aides were sought; Emperor Xiaowu summoned Dai and told him, 「Your fine service has long been plain, and you have already held many offices.
translations.idiomatic: The prince sought men of high rank for his staff; Emperor Xiaowu called Dai in and said, 「Your merit has shown for years, and you have already filled many posts.

sentences.zh: 今欲用卿爲子鸞別駕，總刺史之任，無謂小屈，終當大伸也。

translations.literal: Now I wish to use you as Ziluan's vice administrator, with overall charge of the prefecture—do not call it a small bending; in the end you will be greatly extended.
translations.idiomatic: Now I mean to make you Ziluan's vice administrator with full charge of the prefecture. Do not take it as a slight setback; in time you will rise far higher.

sentences.zh: 」帝崩，累遷吏部郎。

translations.literal: 」When the emperor died, Dai rose in stages to gentleman of the ministry of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: 」After the emperor's death he advanced step by step to gentleman in the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 明帝初，四方反，帝以岱堪幹舊才，除使持節、督西豫州諸軍事、輔國將軍、西豫州刺史。

translations.literal: At the opening of Mingdi's reign, with rebellion on four sides, the emperor judged Dai a man of old capacity and made him bearer of the staff, commander of the military affairs of western Yuzhou, general who supports the state, and inspector of western Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingdi first took the throne and rebellion flared on every side, the emperor deemed Dai a tested man of affairs and named him bearer of the staff, commander of western Yuzhou, general who supports the state, and inspector of western Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋徙爲冠軍將軍、北徐州刺史，都督北討諸軍事，竝不之官。

translations.literal: Soon he was shifted to general of the champion and inspector of northern Xuzhou, commander of the northern campaign forces, and in both cases did not take up the posts.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon moved to general of the champion and inspector of northern Xuzhou, with command of the northern campaign, but never took up either post.

sentences.zh: 泰始末，爲吳興太守。

translations.literal: At the end of the Taishi reign he was administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Taishi reign he served as administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 元徽中，遷使持節、督益寧二州軍事、冠軍將軍、益州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Yuangui era he was shifted to bearer of the staff, commander of the military affairs of Yi and Ning, general of the champion, and inspector of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuangui era he was made bearer of the staff, commander of Yi and Ning, general of the champion, and inspector of Yi.

sentences.zh: 數年，益土安其政。

translations.literal: After several years the people of Yi were at ease under his government.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years the people of Yi had settled under his rule.

sentences.zh: 徵侍中，領長水校尉，度支尚書，領左軍，遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was summoned as palace attendant, concurrently director of the everlasting water guard, revenue superintendent, and commander of the left army, then moved to director of the ministry of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as palace attendant, then held in turn the everlasting water guard, the revenue superintendency, and command of the left army, and was promoted to director of the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 王儉爲吏部郎，時專斷曹事，岱每相違執，及儉爲宰相，以此頗不相善。

translations.literal: Wang Jian was gentleman of the ministry of personnel and then monopolized bureau business; Dai often opposed him, and once Jian became chief minister they were rather ill disposed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian, as gentleman of the ministry of personnel, had long run the bureau on his own; Dai often stood against him, and after Jian rose to chief minister the two were scarcely on good terms.

sentences.zh: 兄子瓌、弟恕，誅吳郡太守劉遐。

translations.literal: His nephew Gui and his younger brother Shu killed Liu Xia, administrator of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Gui and his younger brother Shu killed Liu Xia, administrator of Wu.

sentences.zh: 太祖欲以恕爲晉陵郡，岱曰：「恕未閑從政，美錦不宜濫裁。

translations.literal: The founding emperor wished to give Shu the commandery of Jinling; Dai said, 「Shu is not yet practiced in government; fine brocade should not be cut at random.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor meant to give Shu Jinling commandery; Dai said, 「Shu has not yet learned how to govern—fine brocade should not be hacked at random.

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「恕爲人，我所悉。

translations.literal: 」The founding emperor said, 「Shu as a man—I know him well.
translations.idiomatic: 」The founding emperor said, 「I know Shu's character well enough.

sentences.zh: 且又與瓌同勳，自應有賞。

translations.literal: Moreover he shares merit with Gui; he should by rights receive reward.
translations.idiomatic: And he won his merit beside Gui; reward is only fair.

sentences.zh: 」岱曰：「若以家貧賜祿，此所不論；

translations.literal: 」Dai said, 「If the grant is because the house is poor, that is not in dispute;
translations.idiomatic: 」Dai said, 「If you mean to enrich a poor household, I have nothing to say;

sentences.zh: 語功推事，臣門之恥。」

translations.literal: to speak of merit and push the matter through would be a shame to our gate.」
translations.idiomatic: but to dress it up as reward for merit would disgrace our clan.」

sentences.zh: 世祖卽位，復以岱爲散騎常侍、吳興太守，秩中二千石。

translations.literal: When Shizu took the throne, Dai was again made irregular attendant at court and administrator of Wuxing, with rank at the middle two-thousand-bushel level.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu came to the throne, Dai was again named irregular attendant at court and administrator of Wuxing, with rank at the middle two-thousand-bushel level.

sentences.zh: 岱晚節在吳興，更以寬恕著名。

translations.literal: In his later years Dai was posted at Wuxing and became still more famed for leniency.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Dai held Wuxing and grew still more famous for his leniency.

sentences.zh: 遷使持節監南兖兖徐青冀五州諸軍事、後將軍、南兖州刺史，常侍如故。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Bearer of the Staff supervising military affairs of Nan Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, Rear General, and administrator of Nan Yan; his regular attendant post stood as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to Bearer of the Staff over Nan Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, Rear General, and governor of Nan Yan, while keeping his seat as regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 未拜，卒。

translations.literal: Before he could accept the appointment, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died before he could take up the post.

sentences.zh: 年七十一。

translations.literal: He was seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: He was seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 岱初作遺命，分張家財，封置箱中，家業張減，隨復改易，如此十數年。

translations.literal: Dai early drew up a testament, divided the Zhang family property, and sealed it in chests; as the estate swelled and shrank he revised the division again and again—thus for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Dai made his last wishes, parceling the Zhang family wealth into sealed chests; as the estate waxed and waned he redrew the shares again and again—for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 贈本官，諡貞子。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted his former offices; his posthumous name was Lord of Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: His former offices were granted posthumously; he was given the posthumous name Lord of Integrity.

sentences.zh: 褚炫字彥緒，河南陽翟人也。

translations.literal: Chu Xuan, styled Yanxu, was a native of Yangzhai in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Xuan, styled Yanxu, came from Yangzhai in Henan.

sentences.zh: 祖秀之，宋太常。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xiuzhi was Song Grand Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xiuzhi had been grand minister of ceremonies under the Song.

sentences.zh: 父法顯，鄱陽太守。

translations.literal: His father Faxian was administrator of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Faxian had been administrator of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 兄炤，字彥宣，少秉高節，一目眇，官至國子博士，不拜。

translations.literal: His elder brother Zhao, styled Yanxuan, from youth held lofty integrity; one eye was blind; he reached National University erudite but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Zhao, styled Yanxuan, had been high-minded from youth; blind in one eye, he rose to national university erudite and declined the post.

sentences.zh: 常非從兄淵身事二代，聞淵拜司徒，歎曰：「使淵作中書郎而死，不當是一名士邪！

translations.literal: He often faulted his cousin Yuan for serving two dynasties; when he heard Yuan had been made Grand Commandant, he sighed and said: 「Had Yuan died as Secretariat Director, would he not have been a true gentleman!
translations.idiomatic: He often reproached his cousin Yuan for serving two houses; when he heard Yuan named grand commandant, he sighed: 「If Yuan had died a secretariat director, would he not have died a gentleman?

sentences.zh: 名德不昌，遂令有期頤之壽。」

translations.literal: Fame and virtue did not flourish, and so he was granted a lifespan of a full hundred years.」
translations.idiomatic: Fame and virtue did not bloom—and so he is granted a life to the full hundred.」

sentences.zh: 炫少清簡，爲從舅王景文所知。

translations.literal: Xuan from youth was pure and spare; his maternal uncle Wang Jingwen took note of him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was pure and spare from youth, and his maternal uncle Wang Jingwen marked him early.

sentences.zh: 從兄淵謂人曰：「從弟廉勝獨立，乃十倍於我也。

translations.literal: His cousin Yuan said to others: 「My cousin excels in integrity and stands alone—he is ten times what I am.
translations.idiomatic: Cousin Yuan told others: 「My cousin outdoes me in integrity tenfold—he stands alone where I do not.

sentences.zh: 」宋義陽王昶爲太常，板炫補五官，累遷太子舍人，撫軍車騎記室，正員郎。

translations.literal: 」When Prince of Yiyang Chang of Song was Grand Minister of Ceremonies he recruited Xuan to the Five Offices; he rose through crown prince attendant, staff recorder for the Pacification Army and Flying Cavalry, and regular attendant.
translations.idiomatic: 」When the Prince of Yiyang, Chang of Song, was grand minister of ceremonies he drafted Xuan into the Five Offices; he climbed from crown prince attendant to recorder on the pacification and flying-cavalry staffs, then to regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 從宋明帝射雉，至日中，無所得。

translations.literal: He accompanied Emperor Ming of Song on a pheasant hunt; by midday nothing had been taken.
translations.idiomatic: He went with Emperor Ming of Song to hunt pheasant; by midday the bag was still empty.

sentences.zh: 帝甚猜羞，召問侍臣曰：「吾旦來如皐，遂空行，可笑。

translations.literal: The emperor was deeply suspicious and ashamed, and summoned the attendant ministers: 「I set out this morning for the marshes and came back empty-handed—laughable.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was touchy and ashamed, and called the attendant ministers: 「I rode out this morning for the marsh country and returned with nothing—ridiculous.

sentences.zh: 」座者莫荅。

translations.literal: 」Those seated none answered.
translations.idiomatic: 」No one at the table spoke.

sentences.zh: 炫獨曰：「今節候雖適，而雲露尚凝，故斯翬之禽，驕心未警。

translations.literal: Xuan alone said: 「Though the season is right, clouds and dew still cling, so these brightly plumed birds keep their proud hearts unalert.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan alone said: 「The season is fair, but cloud and dew still hold; these bright-plumed birds keep their pride and have not yet grown wary.

sentences.zh: 但得神駕游豫，羣情便爲載懽。

translations.literal: Only let the divine chariot roam at ease, and all hearts will brim with joy.
translations.idiomatic: Let Your Majesty's sacred carriage roam in ease alone, and every heart will brim with joy.

sentences.zh: 」帝意解，乃於雉場置酒。

translations.literal: 」The emperor's mind eased, and wine was set out at the pheasant field.
translations.idiomatic: 」The emperor's mood lifted, and wine was laid out on the hunting ground.

sentences.zh: 遷中書侍郎，司徒右長史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to secretariat vice director and the grand commandant's right chief aide.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to secretariat vice director and right chief aide to the grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 昇明初，炫以清尚，與劉俁、謝朏、江效入殿侍文義，號爲「四友」。

translations.literal: Early in Shengming, Xuan for his purity joined Liu Yu, Xie Tiao, and Jiang Xiao in the hall to attend literary discussions; they were called the 「Four Friends.」
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Shengming, Xuan's purity won him a place with Liu Yu, Xie Tiao, and Jiang Xiao in the hall for literary discourse—they were called the 「Four Friends.」

sentences.zh: 遷黃門郎，太祖驃騎長史，遷侍中，復爲長史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to gentleman at the Yellow Gate, then chief aide to the Grand Ancestor as marshal; he was made regular attendant and again chief aide.
translations.idiomatic: He became gentleman at the Yellow Gate, then chief aide on the Grand Ancestor's marshal staff; he was named regular attendant and again made chief aide.

sentences.zh: 齊臺建，復爲侍中，領步兵校尉。

translations.literal: When the Qi regime was established he again became regular attendant and held the colonelcy of footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi platform was raised he again sat as regular attendant and held the colonelcy of footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 以家貧，建元初，出補東陽太守，加秩中二千石。

translations.literal: Because his household was poor, in early Jianyuan he was sent out as acting administrator of Dongyang, with rank raised to 2000-dan.
translations.idiomatic: Household poverty sent him out in early Jianyuan as acting governor of Dongyang, with rank raised to 2000-dan.

sentences.zh: 還，復爲侍中，領步兵。

translations.literal: On his return he again became regular attendant and held the footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he again became regular attendant and kept the footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 凡三爲侍中。

translations.literal: Three times in all he was regular attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Three times in all he held regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 出爲竟陵王征北長史，加輔國將軍，尋徙爲冠軍長史、江夏內史，將軍如故。

translations.literal: He was sent out as army chief aide on the Prince of Jingling's Pacify-the-North staff with added rank as general who assists the state; soon he was moved to champion chief aide and interior administrator of Jiangxia, his general's title unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as army chief aide on the Prince of Jingling's Pacify-the-North staff, with added rank as general who assists the state; before long he was shifted to champion chief aide and interior administrator of Jiangxia, still holding his general's title.

sentences.zh: 何戢字慧景，廬江灊人也。

translations.literal: He Ji, styled Huijing, was a native of Qian in Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: He Ji, styled Huijing, came from Qian in Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 祖尚之，宋司空。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shangzhi was Song Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shangzhi had been minister of works under the Song.

sentences.zh: 父偃，金紫光祿大夫，被遇於宋武。

translations.literal: His father Yan was golden-crown deputy grand master and had won favor under Song Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yan was golden-crown deputy grand master and had been favored by Song Wu.

sentences.zh: 選戢尚山陰公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: Ji was chosen to marry the Princess of Shanyin and was named commandant of escort cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was matched to the Princess of Shanyin and named commandant of escort cavalry.

sentences.zh: 解褐祕書郎，太子中舍人，司徒主簿，新安王文學，祕書丞，中書郎。

translations.literal: On leaving lacquer he became secretariat gentleman, crown prince central attendant, grand commandant chief clerk, literary aide to the Prince of Xin'an, secretariat vice director, and secretariat director.
translations.idiomatic: On leaving lacquer he served as secretariat gentleman, crown prince central attendant, grand commandant chief clerk, literary aide to the Prince of Xin'an, secretariat vice director, and secretariat director.

sentences.zh: 景和世，山陰主就帝求吏部郎褚淵入內侍己，淵見拘逼，終不肯從，與戢同居止月餘日，由是特申情好。

translations.literal: In the Jinghe era the Princess of Shanyin asked the emperor to have Chu Yuan of the Ministry of Personnel enter the inner quarters to attend her; Yuan saw himself pressed and would not yield; he lodged with Ji for more than a month, and their bond deepened thereby.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jinghe reign the Princess of Shanyin asked the throne to place Chu Yuan of the ministry of personnel in her inner service; Yuan felt himself cornered and refused; he shared Ji's roof for more than a month, and from that their friendship grew singularly close.

sentences.zh: 明帝立，遷司徒從事中郎，從建安王休仁征赭圻，板轉戢司馬，除黃門郎，出爲宣威將軍、東陽太守，吏部郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne Ji was moved to grand commandant attendant; he followed Prince of Jian'an Xiuren on the Zhuchi campaign, was transferred to Ji as army marshal, named gentleman at the Yellow Gate, then sent out as general who proclaims might and administrator of Dongyang, and made director of the ministry of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming acceded, Ji became grand commandant attendant; he followed Prince of Jian'an Xiuren against Zhuchi, was transferred to Ji as army marshal, named gentleman at the Yellow Gate, then sent out as general who proclaims might and governor of Dongyang, and made director of the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 元徽初，褚淵參朝政，引戢爲侍中，時年二十九。

translations.literal: Early in Yuanhui, Chu Yuan joined in governing and brought Ji in as regular attendant; he was twenty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Yuanhui, Chu Yuan took a hand in government and drew Ji in as regular attendant; he was twenty-nine.

sentences.zh: 戢以年未三十，苦辭內侍，表疏屢上，時議許之。

translations.literal: Because he was not yet thirty Ji earnestly declined inner service; memorials went up again and again, and opinion of the day approved.
translations.idiomatic: Still short of thirty, Ji pressed hard to decline inner service; he sent memorial after memorial, and men of the day thought him right.

sentences.zh: 改授司徒左長史。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as the grand commandant's left chief aide.
translations.idiomatic: He was given instead the grand commandant's left chief aide.

sentences.zh: 戢美容儀，動止與褚淵相慕，時人呼爲「小褚公」。

translations.literal: Ji had a handsome bearing; in movement and deportment he took Chu Yuan as his model, and men of the time called him 「Little Lord Chu.」
translations.idiomatic: Ji was fair of face and figure; in bearing and gait he modeled himself on Chu Yuan, and the age called him 「Little Lord Chu.」

sentences.zh: 家業富盛，性又華侈，衣被服飾，極爲奢麗。

translations.literal: His household was wealthy and his nature lavish; clothing and ornaments were of the utmost luxury.
translations.idiomatic: The house was rich and his taste extravagant; dress and adornment were carried to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 三年，出爲左將軍、吳興太守。

translations.literal: In the third year he was sent out as left general and administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he went out as left general and governor of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 上頗好畫扇，宋孝武賜戢蟬雀扇，善畫者顧景秀所畫。

translations.literal: The sovereign greatly loved painted fans; Emperor Xiaowu of Song had given Ji a cicada-and-sparrow fan painted by the skilled artist Gu Jingxiu.
translations.idiomatic: The throne doted on painted fans; Emperor Xiaowu of Song had once given Ji a cicada-and-sparrow fan by the master Gu Jingxiu.

sentences.zh: 時陸探微、顧彥先皆能畫，歎其巧絕。

translations.literal: At the time Lu Tanwei and Gu Yanxian could both paint, and they marveled at its supreme artistry.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Tanwei and Gu Yanxian were both painters of note, and they gasped at its supreme craft.

sentences.zh: 戢因王晏獻之，上令晏厚酬其意。

translations.literal: Ji offered it up through Wang Yan; the sovereign had Yan richly repay his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Ji presented it through Wang Yan; the throne had Yan reward him handsomely.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he died.

sentences.zh: 時年三十六。

translations.literal: He was thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He was thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 贈散騎常侍、撫軍，太守如故。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted grand master of palace leisure and pacification army; his governorship stood as before.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made grand master of palace leisure and pacification army, still holding his governorship.

sentences.zh: 諡懿子。

translations.literal: His posthumous name was Lord of Grace.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous name Lord of Grace.

sentences.zh: 女爲雞林王后，又贈侍中、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His daughter became queen of Silla; he was again posthumously granted regular attendant and grand master of palace illumination.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter became queen of Silla; he was again granted regular attendant and grand master of palace illumination posthumously.

sentences.zh: 王延之字希季，琅邪臨沂人也。

translations.literal: Wang Yanzhi, styled Xiji, was a native of Langye, Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanzhi, styled Xiji, came from Langye in Linyi.

sentences.zh: 祖裕，宋左光祿儀同三司。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yu was Song Left Grand Master of Splendid Honour with appointments equal to the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yu had served under Song as left grand master of splendid honour with appointments equal to the Three Offices.

sentences.zh: 父昇之，都官尚書。

translations.literal: His father Shengzhi was Director of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shengzhi had been director of justice.

sentences.zh: 延之出繼伯父秀才粲之。

translations.literal: Yanzhi was given in adoption to his father's elder brother, the presented scholar Canzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi was adopted by his father's elder brother, the presented scholar Canzhi.

sentences.zh: 延之少而靜默，不交人事。

translations.literal: In youth Yanzhi was quiet and withdrawn and did not mix in worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Yanzhi was silent and withdrawn, keeping clear of the world's traffic.

sentences.zh: 州辟主簿，不就。

translations.literal: The province summoned him as chief clerk; he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: The province called him to serve as chief clerk; he would not go.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才。

translations.literal: He was recommended as presented scholar.
translations.idiomatic: He was recommended as presented scholar.

sentences.zh: 除北中郎法曹行參軍，轉署外兵尚書外兵部，司空主簿，竝不就。

translations.literal: He was appointed acting adjutant in the north army's law section, transferred to serve in the outer troops section of the Ministry of War, and as master of records under the Minister of Works—all declined.
translations.idiomatic: He was named acting adjutant in the north army's law office, then to the outer-troops section of the war ministry and as master of records under the minister of works—and declined every post.

sentences.zh: 除中軍建平王主簿、記室，仍度司空、北中郎二府，轉祕書丞，西陽王撫軍諮議，州別駕，尋陽王冠軍、安陸王後軍司馬，加振武將軍，出爲安遠護軍，武陵內史，不拜。

translations.literal: He was appointed master of records and recorder for Prince Jianping's central army, then crossed to serve in both the Minister of Works and north army offices, made secretary director, staff adviser to the Prince of Xiyang's pacification army, provincial aide-de-camp, military assistant under the princes of Xunyang and Anlu, with the title Striking Warrior General, and sent out as Protector-General of Pacification and magistrate of Wuling—all refused.
translations.idiomatic: He was made master of records and recorder on Prince Jianping's central-army staff, then passed through the minister of works and north army in turn, became secretary director, adviser on the Prince of Xiyang's pacification army, provincial aide, and military assistant under the princes of Xunyang and Anlu, with the title striking warrior general; when offered protector-general of pacification and magistrate of Wuling, he would not accept.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝爲衞軍，延之轉爲長史，加宣威將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming of Song was general of the guard, Yanzhi became his chief of staff with the title Proclaiming Prestige General.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming of Song held the guard command, Yanzhi became his chief of staff with the title proclaiming prestige general.

sentences.zh: 司徒建安王休仁征赭圻，轉延之爲左長史，加寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: When the Minister of Works, Prince Jian'an Huoren, campaigned at Zhuchi, Yanzhi was made left chief of staff with the title Pacifying the North General.
translations.idiomatic: When the minister of works, Prince Jian'an Huoren, marched on Zhuchi, Yanzhi was shifted to left chief of staff with the title pacifying the north general.

sentences.zh: 延之清貧，居宇穿漏。

translations.literal: Yanzhi lived in austere poverty; his dwelling leaked everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi was poor to the bone; rain came through the roof of his house.

sentences.zh: 褚淵往候之，見其如此，具啓明帝，帝卽敕材官爲起三閒齋屋。

translations.literal: Chu Yuan visited him, saw this condition, and fully reported to Emperor Ming, who at once ordered the works office to erect three study rooms.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yuan called on him, saw how he lived, and laid the matter fully before Emperor Ming, who at once ordered the works office to build him three study rooms.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中，領射聲校尉，未拜，出爲吳郡太守。

translations.literal: He was promoted to palace attendant and concurrently colonel of the archery corps, but before taking office was sent out as governor of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to palace attendant and colonel of the archery corps, but before he could take office was sent out as governor of Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 罷郡還，家產無所增益。

translations.literal: When he left the prefecture and returned, his household possessions had not increased at all.
translations.idiomatic: When he left the prefecture and came home, his household had not grown by a single thing.

sentences.zh: 除吏部尚書，侍中，領右軍，竝不拜。

translations.literal: He was named Minister of Personnel, palace attendant, and commander of the right guard—all declined.
translations.idiomatic: He was named minister of personnel, palace attendant, and commander of the right guard—and would not accept any of them.

sentences.zh: 復爲吏部尚書，領驍騎將軍，出爲後軍將軍、吳興太守。

translations.literal: Again made Minister of Personnel and bold cavalry general, then sent out as rear army general and governor of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Again made minister of personnel and bold cavalry general, then sent out as rear army general and governor of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 遷都督浙東五郡、會稽太守。

translations.literal: He was promoted to supervisor of the five eastern Zhe provinces and governor of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to supervisor of the five eastern Zhe provinces and governor of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 轉侍中，祕書監，晉熙王師。

translations.literal: He was made palace attendant, director of the secretariat, and tutor to the Prince of Jinxi.
translations.idiomatic: He became palace attendant, director of the secretariat, and tutor to the Prince of Jinxi.

sentences.zh: 遷中書令，師如故，未拜，轉右僕射。

translations.literal: He was promoted to director of the Secretariat; his tutorship unchanged; before investing the office, he was shifted to right vice director.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to director of the secretariat while keeping his tutorship, but before he could take office was moved to right vice director.

sentences.zh: 昇明二年，轉左僕射。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengming, he was made left vice director.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengming year two he was made left vice director.

sentences.zh: 宋德旣衰，太祖輔政，朝野之情，人懷彼此。

translations.literal: With Song virtue already failing and the founding emperor holding regency, court and countryside alike split in their loyalties.
translations.idiomatic: Song virtue was already spent; with the founding emperor guiding the state, court and countryside each leaned its own way.

sentences.zh: 延之與尚書令王僧虔中立無所去就，時人爲之語曰：「二王持平，不送不迎。

translations.literal: Yanzhi and the Director Wang Sengqian stayed neutral, cleaving to neither side; people had a saying: 「The two Wangs hold the scales level—they neither see off nor welcome in.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi and the director Wang Sengqian stood in the middle and would not commit; people said of them, 「The two Wangs hold the beam level—they neither see you off nor come to meet you.

sentences.zh: 」太祖以此善之。

translations.literal: 」The founding emperor approved him for this.
translations.idiomatic: 」The founding emperor thought well of him for it.

sentences.zh: 三年，出爲使持節、都督江州豫州之新蔡晉熙二郡諸軍事、安南將軍、江州刺史。

translations.literal: In year three he was sent out with credentials bearing the staff, as supervisor of military affairs in Jiangzhou and the Xincai and Jinxi subprefectures of Yuzhou, as Pacifying South General and inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year three he went out bearing the staff, as supervisor of military affairs in Jiangzhou and the Xincai and Jinxi districts of Yuzhou, pacifying south general and inspector of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 建元二年，進號鎮南將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyuan, his title was raised to Guard-the-South General.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyuan year two his title was raised to guard-the-south general.

sentences.zh: 延之與金紫光祿大夫阮韜，俱宋領軍劉湛外甥，竝有早譽。

translations.literal: Yanzhi and the golden-purple grand master Ruan Tao were both nephews of Song's Director of the Palace Guard Liu Tan, both famed early.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi and the golden-purple grand master Ruan Tao were both nephews of Song's director of the palace guard Liu Tan, and both had won early renown.

sentences.zh: 湛甚愛之，曰：「韜後當爲第一，延之爲次也。

translations.literal: Tan doted on them and said: 「Tao will rank first later; Yanzhi second.
translations.idiomatic: Tan favored them both and said, 「Tao will stand first hereafter; Yanzhi second.

sentences.zh: 」延之甚不平。

translations.literal: 」Yanzhi was deeply aggrieved.
translations.idiomatic: 」Yanzhi took the ranking bitterly to heart.

sentences.zh: 每致餉下都，韜與朝士同例。

translations.literal: Whenever gifts were sent down to the capital, Tao was treated the same as court officials.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever tribute was sent down to the capital, Tao was classed with the men at court.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞其如此，與延之書曰：「韜云卿未嘗有別意，當緣劉家月旦故邪？

translations.literal: The founding emperor heard of this and wrote Yanzhi: 「Tao says you never bore him special ill will—could this be because of the Liu family's monthly ratings?
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor heard of it and wrote Yanzhi, 「Tao tells me you never meant him any slight—could this go back to the Liu family's monthly ratings?

sentences.zh: 」在州祿俸以外，一無所納，獨處齋內，吏民罕得見者。

translations.literal: 」In the province, beyond his salary he accepted nothing; he lived alone in his study, and officials and commoners seldom saw him.
translations.idiomatic: 」In his province he took nothing beyond his salary, kept to his study alone, and officials and commoners seldom laid eyes on him.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷中書令，右光祿大夫，本州大中正。

translations.literal: In year four he was made director of the Secretariat, right grand master of splendid honour, and chief equitable judge of his home province.
translations.idiomatic: In year four he was made director of the secretariat, right grand master of splendid honour, and chief equitable judge of his home province.

sentences.zh: 轉左僕射，光祿、中正如故。

translations.literal: He was shifted to left vice director; his grand master title and chief judgeship were unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to left vice director; his grand master title and chief judgeship stood as before.

sentences.zh: 尋領竟陵王師。

translations.literal: Soon he also served as tutor to the Prince of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he also took charge as tutor to the Prince of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 永明二年，陳疾解職，世祖許之。

translations.literal: In Yongming year two he pleaded illness to resign; the Shizu emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming year two he pleaded illness and asked to leave office; Emperor Shizu allowed it.

sentences.zh: 轉特進，右光祿大夫，王師、中正如故。

translations.literal: He was made extraordinary privy counselor and right grand master; his tutorship and chief judgeship were unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was made extraordinary privy counselor and right grand master; his tutorship and chief judgeship remained as they were.

sentences.zh: 其年卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: That year he died, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he died, at sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 追贈散騎常侍，右光祿大夫、特進如故。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given the office of regular attendant at the scattered cavalry service, with right grand master and extraordinary counselor unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: After death he was given the post of regular attendant at the scattered cavalry service, with right grand master and extraordinary counselor unchanged.

sentences.zh: 諡簡子。

translations.literal: Posthumous title: Master of Refinement.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Master of Refinement.

sentences.zh: 延之家訓方嚴，不妄見子弟，雖節歲問訊，皆先克日。

translations.literal: Yanzhi's household instruction was stern; he would not casually see his sons and nephews—even holiday greetings required a fixed day in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi's household rule was severe: he would not see sons or nephews without cause, and even festival greetings had to be booked in advance.

sentences.zh: 子倫之，見兒子亦然。

translations.literal: His son Lunzhi treated his own sons the same way.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lunzhi dealt with his own sons in the same way.

sentences.zh: 永明中，爲侍中。

translations.literal: During Yongming he served as palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongming reign he served as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 世祖幸琅邪城，倫之與光祿大夫全景文等二十一人坐不參承，爲有司所奏。

translations.literal: When Shizu visited Langye city, Lunzhi and twenty others including the grand master Quan Jingwen were charged for failing to attend the reception.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu visited Langye city, Lunzhi and twenty others, among them the grand master Quan Jingwen, were impeached for failing to attend the imperial progress.

sentences.zh: 詔倫之親爲陪侍之職，而同外惰慢，免官，景文等贖論。

translations.literal: An edict held that Lunzhi held close attendance duty yet shared in outer negligence; he was dismissed from office; Jingwen and others were allowed to pay fines instead.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said Lunzhi held close attendance yet had been as slack as the rest; he was stripped of office, while Jingwen and the others were allowed to redeem their cases with fines.

sentences.zh: 建武中，至侍中，領前軍將軍，都官尚書，領游擊將軍，卒。

translations.literal: During Jianwu he rose to palace attendant, commander of the forward army, director of justice, and raiding army commander, then died.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jianwu he reached palace attendant, commander of the forward army, director of justice, and raiding army commander, then died.

sentences.zh: 阮韜字長明，陳留人，晉金紫光祿大夫裕玄孫也。

translations.literal: Ruan Tao, styled Changming, came from Chenliu, a great-great-grandson of Jin's golden-purple grand master Ruan Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Tao, styled Changming, was of Chenliu, a great-great-grandson of Jin's golden-purple grand master Ruan Yu.

sentences.zh: 韜少歷清官，爲南兖州別駕，刺史江夏王劉義恭逆求資費錢，韜曰：「此朝廷物。

translations.literal: Tao in youth passed through pure offices; as aide-de-camp of southern Yanzhou, when the inspector Prince Jiangxia Liu Yigong demanded funds in advance, Tao said: 「These belong to the court.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Tao rose through clean offices; as aide of southern Yanzhou, when the inspector, Prince Jiangxia Liu Yigong, pressed him for money in advance, Tao said, 「This is the court's property.

sentences.zh: 」執不與。

translations.literal: 」He held firm and would not give them.
translations.idiomatic: 」He stood firm and would not hand it over.

sentences.zh: 宋孝武選侍中四人，竝以風貌。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of Song chose four palace attendants—all for their bearing and looks.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu of Song picked four palace attendants, every one chosen for face and bearing.

sentences.zh: 王彧、謝莊爲一雙，韜與何偃爲一雙。

translations.literal: Wang Yu and Xie Zhuang were one pair; Tao and He Yan were one pair.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu and Xie Zhuang were paired; Tao and He Yan were paired.

sentences.zh: 常充兼假。

translations.literal: He often held concurrent and acting posts.
translations.idiomatic: He was often named to concurrent and acting posts.

sentences.zh: 泰始末，爲征南江州長史。

translations.literal: At the end of Taishi he was chief aide on the Pacify-the-South staff for Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the close of Taishi he served as chief aide to the Pacify-the-South General for Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 桂陽王休範在鎮，數出行遊，韜性方峙，未嘗隨從。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Guiyang, Xiu Fan, held the post, he often went out touring; Tao's nature was upright and stern, and he never followed along.
translations.idiomatic: While the Prince of Guiyang Xiu Fan was in command he went out on pleasure tours again and again; Tao, upright and unyielding by nature, never went along.

sentences.zh: 至散騎常侍，金紫光祿大夫，領始興王師。

translations.literal: He reached Scattered Cavalry Regular Attendant, Household Minister with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and tutored the Prince of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Household Minister with the golden seal and purple ribbon, and preceptor to the Prince of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 永明二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongming he died.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming year 2 he died.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：內侍樞近，世爲華選，金璫熲耀，朝之麗服，久忘儒藝，專授名家。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Inner attendants close to the pivot—for generations a splendid choice; golden clasps blazing bright, the court's fine raiment; long forgetting Confucian arts, grants made only to famous houses.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Palace attendants at the hinge of power were for generations a glittering pick—gold pins ablaze, the court's show-robe; scholarship was long forgotten and posts went only to great clans.

sentences.zh: 加以簡擇少姿，簪貂冠冕，基蔭所通，後才先貌，事同謁者，以形骸爲官，斯違舊矣。

translations.literal: Added to this, selection weighed few on grace of form; marten tails and imperial caps came through family shade; talent followed after appearance; it was the same as chamberlains—taking the bodily frame as the office: this breaches the old way.
translations.idiomatic: Selection besides prized few for beauty: ermine hats and coronets passed by patronage, talent came after looks, and the case matched the chamberlains—men were made officials from their frames alone. That is a breach of the ancient rule.

sentences.zh: 辟強之在漢朝，幼有妙察；

translations.literal: Bi Qiang in the Han dynasty, young, had keen perception;
translations.idiomatic: Bi Qiang in Han times, still a child, read men with sharp sight;

sentences.zh: 仲宣之處魏國，見貶容陋。

translations.literal: Zhongxuan in the Wei state was belittled for an ugly face.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxuan under Wei was scorned for his plain looks.

sentences.zh: 何戢之讓，雖未能深識前古之美，與夫尸官靦服者，何等級哉！

translations.literal: He Zhan's yielding—though he could not deeply know the beauty of antiquity, compared with those who hold office in shame yet wear the robes, what grade is that!
translations.idiomatic: He Zhan's resignations—even without full grasp of the ancients' standard, how many ranks above the men who cling to office in shame and still wear the gown?

sentences.zh: 贊曰：萬石祗慎，琨旣爲倫。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Wan Shi's reverent caution—Kun already became the pattern.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium runs: Wan Shi's wary reverence—Kun already matched that mold.

sentences.zh: 五龍一氏，張亦繼荀。

translations.literal: Five Dragons one clan; Zhang also followed Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Five Dragons in one house; Zhang likewise stood in Xun's mold.

sentences.zh: 炫清褚族，戢遺何姻。

translations.literal: Xuan of the clear Chu clan; Zhan's yield and the He marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Xuan kept the Chu house pure; He Zhan resigned his post yet held the He marriage bond.

sentences.zh: 延之居簡，名峻王臣。

translations.literal: Yanzhi dwelt in simplicity; fame stern—a Wang minister.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi lived simply; a famed and austere minister of Wang.

translations.idiomatic: [1] Endnote marker.
